roles.heroLead: Buyers' inspectors in Lynnwood know exactly where to poke a tiled shower, because tile and grout were never the waterproof part — the membrane underneath is. We build that hidden assembly first, run a 24-hour flood test, photograph the result, and only then set tile. Your 70s rambler gets a shower that outlasts the listing photos.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Lynnwood, WA?
roles.costP1: $14–$26 per square foot installed is the honest range for Lynnwood — tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor combined, with labor alone starting at $11/sq ft. Figure $3,200–$6,800 for a standard tub-shower surround; a complete bathroom with floor, shower and niche typically comes in at $6,500–$14,000, and a bathroom floor by itself (about 45 sq ft) runs $900–$1,600.
roles.costP2: Here's what surprises sellers pricing a pre-listing remodel: the shape of the tile moves your total more than the price sticker does. Installing a $4 mosaic can outcost a $12 large-format porcelain plank, since labor is billed in cuts and grout lines rather than in what the tile cost you.
roles.costNote: Lynnwood ranges, current as of August 2026 — tile, materials and labor combined. The written quote from your free estimate is the number that counts.
roles.layersLead: Bottom to top, seven layers. When a Lynnwood shower fails and we open it up, one of those layers was skipped — nearly always the membrane, saved a few hundred dollars at build time, and the repair now runs five figures.
roles.whyP1: Leaks work quietly. Water slips past grout, wicks into the substrate, and surfaces two years on as a spongy hallway floor or a ceiling stain in the room below — right about when a house goes on the market. At that point you're paying for framing, subfloor, drywall and a complete re-tile.
roles.whyP2: The waterproofing layer is roughly 10% of what a shower costs. Cutting it is the priciest shortcut a bathroom remodel can take.
roles.scopeIntro: These are starting numbers — tile format, substrate condition and layout complexity all push them around. Your real figure gets written on site, free.
roles.cardShower: The whole waterproof build: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, 24-hour flood test, then niche, curb or curbless entry and tile. What you're really buying is the layer nobody sees.
roles.cardFloors: Kitchens, baths, entries, laundry rooms and basements. We flatten the subfloor first and add an uncoupling membrane wherever movement or radiant heat demands it.
roles.cardBacksplash: Herringbone, subway, mosaic sheet or slab-look porcelain. Clean outlet cuts, finished edge trim, grout chosen against your counter rather than off the tile box.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant electric mat set over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested before and after tile, wired to its own circuit. Makes sense only while the floor is already open.
roles.cardRepair: Hollow tiles, crumbling grout, failed shower corners. We'll say plainly whether a repair holds or the substrate underneath is already gone.
roles.cardDemo: Old tile, thinset and backer stripped out behind sheeting and negative air, then hauled away the same day. Your driveway stays clear.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Lynnwood, WA?
roles.faqA1: Expect about $14 to $26 per square foot installed in Lynnwood, covering tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor — labor by itself starts at $11 per square foot. A standard tub-shower surround comes in at $3,200 to $6,800, and a complete bathroom with floor, shower and niche generally runs $6,500 to $14,000. Format drives labor more than the tile's price tag: mosaic sheets and large-format both take noticeably more work per square foot than a plain 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Lynnwood?
roles.faqA2: Plan on $3,200 to $6,800 for a standard alcove shower in Lynnwood — demolition, a bonded waterproofing system, the pre-sloped pan, tile work, a niche and grout all included. Benches, curbless entries, steam setups and full-height stone land above that range. Waterproofing is only about a tenth of the total, and it's the piece that prevents the five-figure failure.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Always. Behind every shower we set goes a bonded waterproofing system — not bare cement board with thinset over it. That means a pre-sloped base, membrane carried up the walls, sealed seams, corners and pipe penetrations, and a 24-hour flood test we document with photos before any tile is placed. Grout and tile shed water; only the membrane actually keeps it out of your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days for a typical Lynnwood bathroom: demolition and dust protection first, then substrate and waterproofing with its 24-hour flood test, one to two days of setting, and a final day for grout, silicone and trim. The shower needs another 24 hours of cure before its first use. A floor on its own is usually a one- to two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: For floors, showers and anything wet or hard-worked, porcelain wins: denser, under 0.5% water absorption, tougher against chips. Ceramic costs less and does fine on walls and backsplashes. In Lynnwood homes we put porcelain on every floor and shower floor and let ceramic or glass make its case on the walls.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: We can, and it's the upgrade listing agents like to mention. Electric radiant mat under tile adds roughly $11 to $16 per square foot installed, thermostat included, and only pencils out while the floor is already open. It sits over an uncoupling membrane, gets a resistance check before and after the tile is set, and takes a dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: In most cases, yes. Demo and haul-away run about $3.50 per square foot, and pulling the old tile is the only way to inspect the subfloor for rot or movement and land the new floor height correctly at doorways. Going over existing tile can work on a flat, sound, well-bonded surface, but it raises the finish height and buries problems better found at demo than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Lynnwood?
roles.faqA8: Figure $1,100 to $2,200 installed for a typical 30 square foot Lynnwood backsplash, with outlet cuts, edge trim and color-matched grout included. Herringbone, mosaic sheets, a framed detail behind the range and slab-look porcelain run to the top of the range — layout and cutting time, not material, is what you're paying for there.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently, yes — repair and regrout start at $8 per square foot. It's the right move when grout is stained or crumbling, an impact cracked a few tiles, or shower corners need grout swapped for silicone. But hollow-sounding tiles, tiles loosening in a pattern, or a wall with give mean the substrate has failed, and a patch only buys months. We tell you which situation is yours before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Lynnwood neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Lynnwood — Alderwood Manor, City Center, South Lynnwood, Scriber Lake, Cedar Valley, College Place, Meadowdale, Perrinville, Martha Lake, Lake Serene, Swamp Creek and Picnic Point — along with Mountlake Terrace, Brier, Edmonds, Mill Creek and the rest of south Snohomish County down to north Seattle.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Tile work from OC Flooring carries a 2-year workmanship warranty — longer than our carpet coverage, because tile problems surface in year two rather than week two. When we install a manufacturer's complete bonded waterproofing assembly, their system warranty applies as well, and the photos of your membrane and flood test become part of the record — handy paperwork when the house sells.
